comments.author: @EpicEarthYTB
comments.text: 🎄 Six cities, countless Christmas lights, and so many beautiful moments — which Christmas market stole your heart? Thank you for sharing this festive journey with me, and if you enjoyed it, please like and subscribe for more adventures with Epic Earth. Merry Christmas, my friends! ❤

comments.author: @peterfillippsss
comments.text:
Hello again Epic Earth, so nice to see your notification pop up.

Wow, that was really impressive, i actually had to watch it twice as there was so much that i found interesting. I`ve always liked how in places where Christmas falls in Winter, people seem to embrace it more. Going out to those night markets would be entertainment all by itself. I guess these markets have been happening for many years and people would really look forward to them. The ice skating rink would be very popular also.

I liked how the footage alternated between the market stalls, the people and then the architecture of the areas. Some of those Grand old buildings were the highlight for me to see. If those buildings could talk, you would find me happily sitting beside the oldest one and listening to the stories it could tell me as to what it has seen in its lifetime. 😊

I`ve just noticed in my feed, a documentary from Epic History, about Nelson`s Battles in Trafalgar from a year ago. Is this your work also. I hope so as i will be keen to watch that being a history buff. 

Thank you once again for your hard work Epic Earth in bringing together another easy to watch and interesting documentary.

I hope your week has been filled with excitement and joy and may each coming week be the same, kind regards

replies.author: @EpicEarthYTB
replies.text:
@peterfillippsss Hello my friend! Reading your reply genuinely touched me to my core—thank you from the bottom of my heart for such an extraordinary message! ❤

Your reflection on celebrating Christmas in the heat of an Australian summer versus those snowy European squares makes so much sense! While a sunny holiday has its own wonderful charm, there is truly an ancient, communal magic in those medieval cobblestone markets that only centuries of shared history can forge.

As for your comparison between 'good' and 'GREAT'—I was honestly at a loss for words. That is one of the most generous, humbling compliments I have ever received. Epic Earth truly is my labor of love, and knowing that this devotion shines through and resonates with you means more than any algorithm or view count ever could. And hearing that you watch all of my documentaries twice to absorb every layer of detail? That is the ultimate badge of honor for an independent creator!

I’m so excited that you discovered the rest of our catalog! Take your time exploring those past journeys—I hope they offer you many more relaxing 'virtual getaways' after your long workdays.

On a more personal note, I would be more than happy to exchange contact info (such as an email) if that’s comfortable and convenient for you. Life is always unpredictable, and who knows what the future holds or how long I’ll be able to keep making these videos. I truly consider you a kindred spirit and a dear friend, and I really wouldn't want to lose touch with you no matter where the journey leads.

Please know that taking the time to reply to you is never a chore—it is genuinely one of the absolute highlights of running this channel. Take wonderful care of yourself, enjoy diving into the older episodes, and until we chat again, warmest regards to you! 🇦🇺✨🎄🙌

replies.author: @peterfillippsss
replies.text:
@EpicEarthYTB Hello Epic Earth
It really is so nice to receive your reply to my replies . I know you must be busy working on the next adventure we will share, but please note your replies are eagerly appreciated.
I like how you have said, centuries of tradition bringing communities together. That is exactly how i see it and probably why i like seeing countries celebrating the festive season together in the cooler climate, because they have been doing it for centuries, maybe is the reason why they seem to be celebrating with such relish. It is nice to see anyway. Coming from a country that is only just over a couple of hundred years old and Christmas being in the middle of a hot summer, we don`t have the traditional celebrations passed on through time as counties in Europe do.
I clicked on your icon yesterday and was pleasantly surprised to see that you have heaps of other documentaries that i have not seen. I will be looking forward to enjoying them when i get the chance. 
I watched the Epic History documentary about Nelson. Although i enjoyed it completely as i had seen other shows regarding Nelson and his time at sea and it interests me, i knew straight away it was not your work. Don`t get me wrong, it was good, but your work i would put in the category  of GREAT. 
You have summed it up in your reply and this is the main reason for my reply to you. What your producing is a, labor of Love, and it shows in your work and is the reason why i find your documentaries so captivating as opposed to just good to watch. I think all of your work i have watched twice as there is so much information to take in and enjoy, that one viewing would not do it justice. So thankyou again for all your hard work Epic Earth, take care of yourself, until we chat again, kind regards 😀

replies.author: @EpicEarthYTB
replies.text:
Hello my friend! Seeing your comment is always the warmest highlight of my week! 😊 Hearing that you enjoyed the European Christmas markets so much that you watched the documentary twice is the greatest compliment an independent creator could ever hope for!

There is truly a special magic when Christmas meets winter in Europe—those cobblestone squares, the glow of market lanterns against the snow, and centuries of tradition bringing communities together in the cold. And your image of sitting beside an ancient building to listen to the stories it could tell… that was pure poetry. Coming from your background in building, you truly appreciate the silent soul within those grand medieval walls.

To answer your question about Epic History: that is actually a completely different and separate channel! While I also have immense respect for their deep dives into military history (and as a history buff, you will certainly love their Nelson documentary!), Epic Earth is my own independent labor of love dedicated to the geography, cultures, landscapes, and wonders of our planet.

Thank you so much for your warmth and loyalty. I hope your week is filled with peace, warmth, and joyful moments. Kindest regards as always! 🎄✨🏰❄️
